meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: adds a reason or an obvious truth

examples.trans: I did tell you, you know!

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'together' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.
I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.en: to call for, to summon (a taxi, driver, police, doctor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to summon', paired with 'вызывать'.

examples.text: Ты же не помнишь ничего. Ты вызвал трезвого водителя!
examples.trans: You don't remember anything, after all. You called a sober driver!

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you
after 2, 3, 4: года; after 5 and more: лет

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

держаться.gloss: to hold on; to stick with

meanings.note: за + accusative: держись за руку = hold on to my hand

meanings.en: to stick with, keep close to
meanings.note: + genitive: держитесь меня = stick with me

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Stick with me and everything will be fine.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё у вас будет хорошо. Потому что я кто?
examples.trans: Stick with me, and everything will be fine for you. Because who am I?

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: to run for a second term

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: also a flat number in an address

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?
All right, here you go. There, look.
I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

отдохнуть.gloss: to have a rest; to relax

examples.trans: You need to have a proper rest at home.

examples.text: Иди уже скорее домой, пора хорошенько отдохнуть.
examples.trans: Go home already quickly, it is time to have a good rest.

examples.text: Ложись спать, тебе надо хорошо отдохнуть.
examples.trans: Go to sleep, you need to rest well.

examples.text: Я же тебе говорил: пошли оттуда!
examples.trans: I told you: let us leave that place!

examples.text: Надо было силой меня оттуда уводить!
examples.trans: You should have dragged me away from there by force!
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: + infinitive: Пора идти = Time to go

examples.trans: It's time for us to go.
All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: по порядку = in order; всё в порядке = everything is fine

examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order.

examples.text: Теперь давай всё по порядку. Скажи мне, сколько ты им должна?
examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order. Tell me, how much do you owe them?

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?
How much power does this car have?

examples.text: Да, по-моему, здорово! Сколько сил в этой машине?
examples.trans: Yes, I think it's great! How much power does this car have?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

examples.text: Ты точно в порядке, может, вызвать такси?
examples.trans: Are you definitely alright, maybe call a taxi?
The taxi already drove up to the house.
We called a cab to the station.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?
We give him three days. That's it.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'mother-in-law (wife's mother)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Если бы вы моей тёщей были, я бы терпел.
examples.trans: If you were my mother-in-law, I would put up with you.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, если бы вы моей тёщей были! Тогда я бы терпел.
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, if you were my mother-in-law! Then I would put up with you.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, если бы вы моей тёщей были!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, if you were my mother-in-law!

уводить.gloss: to lead away; to drag away

meanings.note: to guide or take away from a place

examples.text: Надо было силой меня оттуда уводить!
examples.trans: You should have dragged me away from there by force!

examples.text: Это слово «уводить» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to lead away' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

examples.text: Ладно, Рожок с тобой, не унывай сейчас.
examples.trans: Alright, Rozhok is with you, do not despair right now.

examples.text: Это слово «унывать» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to despair' is often heard in conversation.
You need to have a proper rest at home.

examples.text: Иди уже скорее домой, пора хорошенько отдохнуть.
examples.trans: Go home already quickly, it is time to have a good rest.

examples.text: Значит, нам обоим нужно хорошенько подумать.
examples.trans: So, both of us need to think carefully.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do you want me to tell you honestly?

examples.text: Всё честно, Лёха. Взрослые не умеют ждать.
examples.trans: It's all fair, Lyokha. Grown-ups can't wait.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
